claims.claim: 4 models: Fable 5.1, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Haiku 4.5.
claims.truth: The current models are Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5. Which ones you can pick depends on your plan.
claims.source_title: Change the model, effort and thinking settings

claims.claim: Always select Opus 4.6. It's the smartest model available. Period.
claims.truth: Opus 4.6 has been replaced, and Fable 5.1 now sits above Opus. "Always" is also opinion: the right model depends on the task, and lighter models are faster for simple work.
claims.source_title: Change the model, effort and thinking settings

claims.claim: Haiku: do not use it. Use ChatGPT instead.
claims.truth: One author's preference. Haiku is Anthropic's fastest model, built for quick, light tasks. Whether it suits you depends on what you're doing.

claims.claim: Extended thinking works everywhere. Always turn it on.
claims.truth: On current models, thinking is adaptive and can't be switched off in the Claude app; you control how hard Claude works with the Effort setting, from Low to Max. Anthropic recommends keeping the defaults for everyday work rather than maxing everything out.
claims.source_title: Change the model, effort and thinking settings

claims.claim: 1M token context window.
claims.truth: On paid plans, Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5 have a 1-million-token context window in chat, and every listed model gets 1M in Claude Code. The help article doesn't cover the Free plan.
claims.source_title: How large is the context window on paid Claude plans?

claims.claim: The model matters more than the prompt. A bad prompt on Opus beats a great prompt on Haiku.
claims.truth: A rule of thumb, not a tested fact. A stronger model helps with hard problems, but a clear prompt improves results on every model.

claims.claim: Claude: 245 million users.
claims.truth: No Anthropic page gives a total user count. The figure circulates on third-party statistics sites.

claims.claim: You need Pro ($20/month) or $17/month annually.
claims.truth: Pro is $20 a month, or $17 a month billed annually ($200 up front). Many features also work on the Free plan.

claims.claim: Claude Cowork and Projects both need a Pro plan ($20/mo).
claims.truth: Free accounts can create up to five projects. Paid plans remove the cap, and Team and Enterprise add project sharing.

claims.claim: Chat: no memory of your identity. Every chat starts blank.
claims.truth: Memory from chat history is available on every plan, including Free, and keeps each project's memory separate. Searching past chats requires a paid plan. Both are managed in Settings under Capabilities.
claims.source_title: Use Claude's chat search and memory

claims.claim: Set Global Instructions once: Settings → Cowork → Edit Global Instructions.
claims.truth: The account-wide setting is now called Instructions for Claude, found in Settings. Projects have their own instructions on top of that.

claims.claim: Cowork is desktop only (click the Cowork tab).
claims.truth: Anthropic has folded these file-working capabilities into Claude itself, though a few Anthropic pages still use the Cowork name. Claude runs on the web, desktop, and mobile, and some features need the desktop app.

claims.claim: Connectors are free on all plans. Every paid plan has them.
claims.truth: Connectors from the directory work on every plan, including Free. Free accounts are limited to one custom connector, and on Team and Enterprise an owner enables each connector first.
claims.source_title: Use connectors to extend Claude's capabilities

claims.claim: Settings → Connectors → Browse → Click "Add."
claims.truth: Connectors moved to Customize: open Customize, then Connectors, click +, pick one, click Connect, and sign in to that service.
claims.source_title: Use connectors to extend Claude's capabilities

claims.claim: 50+ connectors available.
claims.truth: The official directory now lists far more: 829 when checked. Every app the sheets named (Slack, Google Drive, Gmail, Calendar, Notion, Figma, Canva, Gamma, Granola) has one.

claims.claim: 11 official plugins: Sales, Marketing, Legal, Finance, Data, Product, Support, and more.
claims.truth: There's no fixed count; Anthropic describes a growing library. Plugins need a paid plan and are installed under Customize, then Plugins. They can bundle skills, commands, connectors, and more.

claims.claim: A skill is a task you teach Claude once. Customize → Skills, toggle on. Type /name or just ask.
claims.truth: Accurate. Skills work on every plan, including Free, with code execution turned on. Claude mostly picks up relevant skills on its own; typing / to choose one also works. Asking Claude to build a skill uses its built-in skill-creator.

claims.claim: Share artifacts with non-Claude users.
claims.truth: Shared artifact links require viewers to have a Claude account. Only published legacy chat artifacts open for anyone with the link.

claims.claim: Claude in Excel: Insert → Get Add-ins → search "Claude by Anthropic." Nothing happens without your approval.
claims.truth: It's now the Claude for Microsoft 365 add-in, installed from Microsoft AppSource or deployed by an admin, and it needs a paid plan. Claude can edit cells directly; it asks you to confirm risky changes and warns before overwriting data.

claims.claim: Claude is not best at real-time search. Use Grok (connected to X).
claims.truth: Claude has built-in web search on every plan, including Free. Turn it on from the tools menu in the chat box.

claims.claim: Claude is not best at images. Use ChatGPT for images.
claims.truth: Claude doesn't generate photos or illustrations the way image tools do. It can build diagrams, charts, and interactive visuals, and it can read images you upload.

claims.claim: Add "Use AskUserQuestion before starting." It generates clickable buttons to select.
claims.truth: AskUserQuestion is documented for Claude Code and Anthropic's Agent SDK: Claude asks up to four questions with clickable options, and you can type your own answer. Asking Claude to ask clarifying questions works in any Claude app.

claims.claim: Start every prompt with "Use ASD-STE100."
claims.truth: ASD-STE100 is a real standard, Simplified Technical English, written for aerospace manuals. Asking for plain, simple language can help, but this is one author's technique, not Anthropic guidance.

claims.claim: Keep your files under 200 lines. Long files eat context; shorter is better.
claims.truth: A personal rule of thumb. Current models handle very large inputs; concise, well-organized instructions help most.

claims.claim: Claude takes 1 to 7 minutes per task.
claims.truth: Task time varies widely with the request, the model, and the effort level. No official source gives a typical range.

claims.claim: Download the desktop app at claude.com/download.
claims.truth: That's the official download page, with macOS, Windows, a Linux beta, and mobile links.

claims.claim: Tab: toggle extended thinking.
claims.truth: Tab now accepts autocomplete. In Claude Code, thinking is toggled with Option+T on a Mac or Alt+T elsewhere, and it has no effect on models that always think.

claims.claim: "Think harder" forces high effort; "Ultra think" forces maximum reasoning.
claims.truth: "Think harder" is read as ordinary text. The documented keyword is ultrathink, one word, which asks for deeper reasoning on that turn. /effort changes the level for the session.

claims.claim: /fork renamed to /branch (alias kept).
claims.truth: Both now exist and do different things. /branch switches you into a copy of the conversation; /fork copies it into a separate background session while you keep working.

claims.claim: /fast: toggle fast mode (Opus 4.6 at 2.5x speed).
claims.truth: Fast mode still runs up to 2.5x faster at a higher price, but on newer Opus models, not 4.6.

claims.claim: /loop: run a prompt on a recurring schedule.
claims.truth: Accurate: /loop repeats a prompt within a Claude Code session, useful for quick polling. For schedules that keep running when your computer is off, Claude Code has cloud routines.
claims.source_title: Claude Code: run prompts on a schedule

claims.claim: /init: auto-generate a CLAUDE.md for your project.
claims.truth: Accurate. /init drafts a CLAUDE.md that Claude Code reads at the start of every session.
